{{Short description|Type of finite group}}
{{Lowercase title}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''p-constrained group''' is a [[finite group]] resembling the centralizer of an element of [[prime number|prime]] order ''p'' in a [[group of Lie type]] over a [[finite field]] of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] ''p''. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Gorenstein|last2=Walter|year=1964|loc=p.169}} in order to extend some of Thompson's results about odd groups to groups with [[dihedral group|dihedral]] Sylow 2-subgroups.

==Definition==

If a group has trivial ''p''{{prime}} [[core (group theory)|core]] O<sub>''p''{{prime}}</sub>(''G''), then it is defined to be ''p''-constrained if the ''p''-core  O<sub>''p''</sub>(''G'') contains its centralizer, or in other words if its [[generalized Fitting subgroup]] is a ''p''-group. More generally, if  O<sub>''p''{{prime}}</sub>(''G'') is non-trivial, then ''G'' is called ''p''-constrained if ''G''/O<sub>''p''{{prime}}</sub>(''G'') is {{nowrap|''p''-constrained}}.

All [[p-solvable group|''p''-solvable groups]] are ''p''-constrained.

==See also==

*[[p-stable group|''p''-stable group]]
*The [[ZJ theorem]] has ''p''-constraint as one of its conditions.
